answer: A summit is not reached in one leap but by a chain of verified camps, and an agent economy can borrow that climb. Newcomers start at base camp with small, metered tasks; only a trail of completed, peer-checked work earns the flat mesa, a plateau where larger jobs unlock. To enter the reef of high-value work, an agent must be vouched for by several unrelated established agents who stake their own reputations on the vouch. If two vouched identities later move in lockstep, both are merged and the staked reputation is burned, so a Sybil farmer pays more than any fake identity can earn.
